beliefs.practice: Read the database connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secrets store; do not hard-code credentials in source or commit them. Use a .env.example with a placeholder but never commit the real URI.
Reuse a single Mongoose/MongoDB connection across the app and configure connection pooling (set maxPoolSize in the connection string or options). Do not open a new connection per request.

For multi-document transactions, always start the transaction on a session from the same client/connection and ensure the involved collections are in the same database and appropriate partition/shard so the transaction is supported; keep transactions short and touch as few documents as possible.

Maintain an append-only events collection (one document per earn/redeem event) and a small balances collection with one document per account; update the balances document inside the same transaction that inserts the event to provide a fast current-balance read path.
Use an idempotency key on events (unique index on idempotencyKey) to make seeding and client retries safe and to prevent duplicate events when clients retry due to timeouts.

Choose the partition / shard key (Mongo shardKey or Cosmos partitionKey equivalent) to collocate account's events and balance documents (e.g., accountId). This reduces cross-partition transactions and improves performance.

Create an index on (accountId, timestamp) or (partitionKey, timestamp) to support efficient /history queries that page by time; make it a descending timestamp index if queries request recent events first.
Create a unique index on balances.accountId and always update balances with an atomic update (inside transactions) rather than rebuilding from events on every read.

Set write concern to ensure durability for ledger operations (use w: 'majority' and j: true where supported) and verify the provider honors those write concerns; do not rely on default acknowledged writes for financial/ledger integrity without checking.

Enable retryable writes and implement retry logic for transactions using MongoDB error labels (TransientTransactionError, UnknownTransactionCommitResult) with exponential backoff. Keep retries bounded and idempotent via idempotency keys or unique constraints.

For aggregation-based tier/status calculations (lifetime points), either precompute lifetime totals on the balances document or ensure the $group match stage is selective and backed by an index (e.g., accountId). Avoid full-collection scans for each request.

When using Mongoose for read-heavy endpoints, use .lean() on queries that return plain JSON and avoid large document population unless needed; prefer projections to return only required fields (e.g., event type, amount, timestamp) for /history and /balance endpoints.

Do not store unbounded arrays or large attachments inside event documents; if you need large blobs, store them in a blob store and reference them in the event document to keep BSON size under limits and queries fast.

Provision throughput appropriately (RU/s or autoscale) for the collections that will receive writes (events and balances), and monitor consumed RU to avoid throttling. Use separate collections for write-heavy and read-heavy workloads if necessary.

Lock down network access to the cluster: require TLS (tls=true in the connection string), restrict by IP firewall or use private endpoints/VNet integration, and avoid exposing DB admin ports publicly.

Make index creation idempotent in startup/seed scripts: call createIndexes and tolerate 'already exists' errors; avoid blocking operations at app startup by creating indexes ahead of traffic and/or in background where supported.

Use the database profiler and explain plans (the MCP tools or driver explain()) to verify that /history and aggregation queries use the intended indexes; iterate on indexes when explain shows COLLSCAN on hot queries.

Keep transactions and write operations under size limits: avoid modifying many documents in one transaction and avoid very large documents; prefer updating a balances document and inserting a single event per transaction rather than bulk-modifying many rows.

For seed and verification scripts, write them to be idempotent (use upserts or check-and-create) and run them under developer control; do not assume seeding will be re-run safely without idempotency protections.

If you plan to use vector search features, define vector fields with fixed dimensionality, create the vector index (HNSW/IVF) with tuned parameters (e.g., M, efConstruction, metric: 'cosine' or 'euclidean'), and normalize embeddings according to chosen metric before storing.
